title: ABM Pilot (Regulated Workloads): Intent Signal Sources + Scoring Notes
body:
Context
- This doc is for the 6–8 week Vertical ABM pilot (regulated workloads; initial focus: financial services + healthcare).
- Goal: interpret “intent signals” consistently across Marketing + Sales so we don’t over-rotate on noisy activity and we move fast on real buying motion (security review, VPC/on-prem requirements, procurement engagement).
- This is NOT a generic PLG scoring model. It’s tuned for: (a) named accounts list, (b) compliance-driven buyers, (c) Dedicated + Private deployment motions.

Operating principles (please read)
1) Account-level > lead-level in ABM
- A single person downloading a benchmark does not equal an opportunity.
- We score both “Contact Intent” and “Account Intent.” The account score is what drives prioritization/routing.

2) Signal = (Strength) x (Fit) x (Freshness)
- Strength: what happened (security review request > blog page view)
- Fit: who did it (CISO/IT Sec/Platform Eng > student/personal email) + account tier
- Freshness: new activity matters more; we apply decay.

3) Regulated workloads have “high-friction” signals
- The strongest buying signals look like work: evidence pack request, questionnaire, architecture review, private networking questions, procurement/legal involvement.

4) Don’t create compliance risk in outreach
- Scoring is internal-only. Do not reference specific tracking behavior to prospects (“saw you looked at X”) in a way that feels invasive.

Definitions
- Target accounts: the named account list in the pilot sheet (FinServ + Healthcare).
- Personas (priority):
  A) CISO / Security leadership / GRC
  B) Platform / Infrastructure / ML Engineering (owns deployment)
  C) Procurement / Vendor mgmt / Legal (appears late, but very high-intent)
- Deployment motions:
  - Dedicated: isolated capacity + SLA; often the “fastest path” for regulated teams that can accept Redwood-managed infra.
  - Private: VPC/on-prem; highest intent when data boundaries + residency + control plane requirements are explicit.

Data sources we’ll use
- Website + docs analytics (UTM-tagged sessions; account enrichment via Clearbit/6sense-style matching where available; otherwise by self-identification via forms)
- HubSpot (forms, email engagement, lifecycle stage)
- LinkedIn (ads + outbound touches; captured as “soft intent” unless it leads to a meeting)
- Partner referrals (AWS co-sell, marketplace private offer inbound, SI introductions)
- Sales activity (meetings booked, replies, discovery notes)
- Security workflow (questionnaire received, evidence pack requested/shared, security review scheduled)

Scoring model (v0.3 for pilot)
- Two scores:
  1) Contact Intent Score (0–100+)
  2) Account Intent Score = top 3 contacts’ scores + “Account Motion” bonuses
- Decay:
  - Soft signals (web, ads): decay 50% after 14 days of no activity
  - Medium signals (content downloads, webinar attendance): decay 50% after 30 days
  - Hard signals (security review, questionnaire, procurement): no decay during pilot window (we treat as active until explicitly closed-lost)

A) Signal catalog + points (strength)

HARD INTENT (fast follow-up; usually means real project)
- Security questionnaire received (customer sends their template) -> +60 (Account Motion bonus +40)
- Evidence pack request (SOC2, pen test summary process, encryption diagrams, audit log sample) -> +50 (Account Motion bonus +30)
- Security review meeting scheduled -> +45 (Account Motion bonus +25)
- Procurement/legal call requested OR redlines sent -> +60 (Account Motion bonus +50)
- “Needs VPC/on-prem / private networking required” stated in writing (email/call notes) -> +50
- Pilot/POC request (explicit timeline + success criteria) -> +70 (Account Motion bonus +40)
- Architecture deep dive requested (SSO/SAML, audit export, KMS/HSM, log retention) -> +40

MEDIUM INTENT (take seriously; qualifies for targeted outreach)
- Regulated landing page form fill (Request demo / Contact us) -> +35
- “Benchmark/Pilot plan” doc download (gated) -> +30
- Webinar registration (attended live) -> +25
- Webinar registration (no-show) -> +10
- Reply to outbound email with non-trivial question (not a brush-off) -> +25
- Meeting booked (discovery) -> +35
- Multiple stakeholders engaged (2+ personas) within 21 days -> +20 (Account Motion bonus +15)

SOFT INTENT (directional; do not over-weight)
- Regulated landing page view (>= 60 sec) -> +6
- Private deployments / dedicated pricing + packaging page view -> +8
- Security FAQ page view -> +8
- Docs page view: audit logs / SAML / KMS keywords -> +8
- 3+ sessions from same corporate domain within 7 days -> +10
- LinkedIn ad click -> +3
- LinkedIn ad form fill -> +15
- Outbound email open -> +1 (cap at +3/week)
- Outbound email click -> +4

NEGATIVE / DISQUALIFYING ADJUSTMENTS
- Student/personal email domain + no matching account -> -25
- Job function clearly non-buyer for this motion (e.g., “student”, “consultant” w/ no client named) -> -15
- Competitor email domain -> set to 0 and flag for review
- “We don’t do cloud / no external vendors” -> -40
- Explicit closed-lost reason captured (timing, build vs buy, standardizing elsewhere) -> set Account Intent to 0 and mark as “Closed – Nurture”

B) Fit multipliers (who + what)
- Persona multiplier (applies to Contact Intent Score):
  - CISO / Security / GRC: x1.4
  - Platform/Infra/ML Eng: x1.2
  - Product/Innovation: x1.0
  - Procurement/Legal: x1.3 (late-stage weight)
  - Other/unknown: x0.8

- Account tier multiplier (applies to Account Intent Score):
  - Tier 1 (top ABM accounts): x1.3
  - Tier 2: x1.1
  - Tier 3: x1.0

C) Account Motion bonuses (what indicates coordinated buying)
- Two different priority personas engaged within 14 days -> +20
- Security + Platform both engaged within 21 days -> +30
- “Private deployment required” + security evidence request -> +30
- Partner referral (AWS co-sell / SI intro) -> +25

Thresholds + routing rules (pilot SLAs)
- Account Intent Score >= 120 OR any HARD INTENT signal present:
  - Route: AE + SE assist (Markus/Fatima coverage depending on region)
  - SLA: 24 hours for first human follow-up
  - Next step: propose (a) security review call, or (b) 30-min architecture screen, or (c) 2-week benchmark/pilot plan

- Account Intent Score 70–119 (medium):
  - Route: AE owns, SDR supports with persona mapping + sequences
  - SLA: 48 hours
  - Next step: meeting ask anchored on regulated outcomes (auditability + predictable latency/cost + deployment controls)

- Account Intent Score 30–69 (warm/early):
  - Route: Marketing nurture + light AE touches (1–2) if tier 1
  - SLA: weekly review only
  - Next step: offer webinar or “security FAQ + evidence pack index” (do not send restricted artifacts without gating)

- Account Intent Score < 30:
  - Route: no action unless it’s a named Tier 1 account; keep in ads + retargeting

How Sales/Marketing should interpret common patterns

Pattern 1: “Security FAQ traffic spike”
- Meaning: could be genuine buyer research OR generic curiosity.
- What to check:
  - Is the domain a target account? Are there multiple sessions / multiple people?
  - Did they also view Private/Dedicated pages or audit log docs?
- Recommended action:
  - If target account: AE sends a short note offering a security Q&A + provides the public Security FAQ link.
  - Avoid: “saw you reading our security page.” Instead: “We often get questions on audit logs, SSO/SAML, KMS; happy to walk through.”

Pattern 2: Benchmark download + no reply
- Meaning: evaluation / internal comparison. Medium intent.
- What to check:
  - Did they view pricing/packaging afterwards? Any second stakeholder?
- Recommended action:
  - SDR follow-up with “what are you benchmarking (latency, cost, throughput, deployment constraints)?”
  - Offer a 30-min performance + deployment screen.

Pattern 3: Evidence pack request early
- Meaning: very high intent; security is gating the deal.
- Recommended action:
  - Loop in Security (Naomi/Daniel/Olga) immediately.
  - Confirm scope of request + NDA status + sharing method.
  - AE should run mutual action plan with dates (security review -> technical deep dive -> pilot -> procurement).

Pattern 4: Partner intro (AWS)
- Meaning: higher than average conversion if tied to Marketplace/private offer and a named workload.
- Recommended action:
  - Tag for co-sell, capture partner source in HubSpot, and align on who owns next meeting.

Pattern 5: Lots of ad clicks, low-quality form fills
- Meaning: audience too broad or creative misaligned.
- Recommended action:
  - Marketing adjusts targeting to job functions and company size; add more “security review / VPC” qualifiers on forms.

HubSpot fields + conventions (so we can actually measure)
- Required fields to set when possible:
  - Target Account (Y/N)
  - ABM Tier (1/2/3)
  - Primary Persona (Security / Platform / Procurement / Other)
  - Primary Vertical (FinServ / Healthcare / Other)
  - Source Detail (Outbound email, LinkedIn ads, Website inbound, Partner referral, Event/webinar)
  - Intent Stage (Soft / Medium / Hard)
  - Next Step (Discovery, Security review, Technical deep dive, Pilot scoping, Procurement)

- UTM conventions (Marketing):
  - utm_campaign: abm_regulated_wk{week#}_{vertical}
  - utm_source: linkedin | email | partner | organic
  - utm_content: ad_{variant} | seq_{touch#} | webinar_{name}

- Notes discipline (Sales):
  - When a HARD INTENT event happens, add the phrase “HARD_INTENT: <type>” to the activity note.
  - Example: “HARD_INTENT: evidence pack request (SOC2 + audit log sample); NDA pending; security review requested next week.”

Quality control + common failure modes
- False positives:
  - IP-based company matching can misattribute traffic (VPNs, shared networks). Treat web-only signals as soft until corroborated.
  - Consulting firms browsing for multiple clients: require named account confirmation.

- Duplicate contacts:
  - Merge duplicates when they show up as “Firstname Lastname (Personal)” + “Firstname Lastname (Work).”

- Over-scoring “opens/clicks”:
  - Opens/clicks are useful for copy testing, not for deal motion.

Weekly cadence for the pilot (how we’ll use this)
- Mondays (Marketing Ops + Sales Ops): refresh account intent snapshot (Top 20 by score + any HARD INTENT flags)
- Tuesdays (ABM standup): pick 5–10 accounts for focused pushes (outreach + partner asks + content)
- Thursdays: review conversions (meeting booked, security review scheduled, pilots started) and adjust point weights if we’re misclassifying

Appendix: Quick scoring examples

Example A (FinServ target)
- 2 people from target domain view Regulated landing page (+10) + Security FAQ (+16) + Private deployments page (+8)
- One fills “Request demo” (+35) and job title is “Director, InfoSec” (x1.4)
- Contact intent approx: (35 + 6 + 8) * 1.4 ≈ 68.6
- Account intent adds second stakeholder activity + persona bonus -> likely crosses 70–119 (medium) even before any security call.

Example B (Healthcare target)
- Platform Eng attends webinar live (+25, x1.2)
- Follow-up email asks about VPC + audit log retention (+25)
- Requests evidence pack (+50) -> HARD INTENT
- Account intent immediately routes to AE+SE with 24h SLA.

Open questions (to resolve during pilot)
- Do we want to treat “SAML/SCIM edge case question” as HARD intent (+40) or MEDIUM (+25) when it comes in via support-style channels?
- For Healthcare: do we need an extra modifier for explicit PHI handling language (“PHI present”) vs “PHI-adjacent”?
- Should partner referrals get a higher bonus when the partner confirms there is an active funding/project timeline?

Changelog
- 2025-04-29: v0.1 draft created (Tyler)
- 2025-05-06: v0.2 added HARD INTENT buckets + decay rules; aligned to pilot metrics spec
- 2025-05-16: v0.3 clarified thresholds/routing + added HubSpot notes discipline (pending final sign-off from Sales Ops + Growth)
